description: Cross-compiler trajectory conformance (CONFORMANCE_SPEC.md §5.44). Every compiler a binding offers must reproduce the Julia `interpreter` trajectory of the same document within the fixture's written band, or refuse it by name. Fixtures are referenced by path from the existing simulation tiers; nothing is authored here. `golden/<id>.json` is the Julia interpreter's trajectory for each fixture, minted with `--write-golden --bindings julia --compiler interpreter`.

interpreter.note: Complete over the evaluable core (esm-libraries-spec §2.5.10), so a refusal here is always red, whatever a fixture's `required` map says.

native.note: The strict default. Julia's strict build has landed, so julia must ANSWER for `native`; rust and python stay optional until theirs do and cross on the same one-way ratchet. A REFUSAL is governed by each fixture's `required` map, not by this list.

xla.note: OPTIONAL for every binding, because `xla` is the compiler that needs a HEAVY EXTERNAL DEPENDENCY and no producer stage for it is wired into scripts/test-conformance.sh. Julia's `esm_problem(…; compiler = :xla)` has landed and answers for all six fixtures against the golden and their anchors with no refusals — run it with `--bindings julia --compiler xla`, whose adapter environment is scripts/compiler_agreement_reactant_env — but `bindings_required` makes an `unavailable` RED, and until the stage runs in the gate that would only mean red for a checkout whose Reactant environment did not instantiate. Julia crosses on the same one-way ratchet `native` used once the stage is wired. Rust needs the `xla` feature and XLA_EXTENSION_DIR. Unconfigured is `unavailable`, not `refused`.

mtk.note: Julia only; needs ModelingToolkit loaded. The one compiler that runs events and implicit equations.

scope_excluded.typescript: no Problem type, so no compiler to name (API_SPEC.md §3, capability profiles)
scope_excluded.go: no Problem type, so no compiler to name (API_SPEC.md §3, capability profiles)

excluded.reason: precision-changing; excluded until every compiler lowers a precision change (CONFORMANCE_SPEC §5.38.4, ruling 2026-09-13). The `float32` class is carried above for when it is included.

tolerance.detail: copied from tests/conformance/pde_simulation/manifest.json `tolerances.traj_golden_rtol` / `traj_golden_atol`, which that tier carries tier-wide

anchor.detail: that tier's `trajectory.analytic` block at the same save times; gated at its `traj_analytic_rtol` / `traj_analytic_atol`

trajectory.detail: `tspan`, `initial_conditions` and the save times come from the model's inline `tests` entry; the assertion times are the save times.

tolerance.integration_factor_detail: the §5.44.2 integration safety factor: a solver's reltol/abstol bound its LOCAL error per step, while the value compared here carries the GLOBAL error, which exceeds it by an integrator-dependent factor. Without it the band demands that every binding's integrator beat a promise no integrator makes, and two correct integrators read as a compiler disagreement. 100x on 1e-10 is still six orders below any compiler-level defect.
tolerance.detail: a method-of-lines stencil is a fold, and this fixture's interior rows cancel exactly; the scaled floor is what makes an exact zero comparable (CONFORMANCE_SPEC §5.38.2)

anchor.detail: the inline test's assertions are the discrete eigenvalue solution, computed outside every binding; gated at the assertion's own declared tolerance
